gpb_detect_tip: Adds the GPIB boards seen by the VISA libraries and the serial ports that look like a Prologix/AR488
gpb_board_tip: Interface number: 0 for GPIB0. Shown in Keysight Connection Expert or NI MAX (on Linux: the minor in /etc/gpib.conf)
gpb_port_tip: Serial port (COM5, /dev/ttyUSB0) or IP of the GPIB-ETHERNET (192.168.1.20 or 192.168.1.20:1234)
gpb_scan_timeout_tip: Wait for each address during the scan: raise it for slow instruments
gpb_idn_tip: Tried in turn, comma separated: *IDN? for SCPI instruments, ID? for older HP ones
gpb_detected: Adapters added: {count}. Check them and press Save.
gpb_overall_warn: Adapter probably usable: read the warnings
gpb_overall_error: Adapter not usable: follow the hints
gpb_scan_empty: [GPIB-004] No instrument answers on {adapter} ({count}): check cables, addresses and power
gpb_col_resource: Address to use in the project
gpb_no_idn: (present, does not answer the identification commands)
gpb_select_device: Select an instrument in the table first
gpb_ifc_tip: Resets the bus: every instrument stops talking/listening
gpb_local_tip: Releases the REN line: the instruments go back to front-panel control
gpb_pick_none: No known instrument for this adapter: press Scan now
diag_no_pyvisa: [GPIB-002] pyvisa is not installed (pip install pyvisa pyvisa-py)
diag_no_pyserial: [GPIB-002] pyserial is not installed (pip install pyserial)
diag_usb_missing: {adapter} not found on the USB bus: check the cable
diag_usb_unknown: USB devices cannot be listed on this system: check skipped
diag_no_firmware: [GPIB-003] {adapter} is connected but its firmware is not loaded ({ids})
diag_board_found: Board GPIB{board} found with the VISA library '{backend}'
diag_board_missing: Board GPIB{board} not found with the VISA library '{backend}' (boards seen: {boards})
diag_board_not_found: [GPIB-001] the adapter is not seen as GPIB{board} by any VISA library
diag_py_no_gpib: pyvisa-py cannot use GPIB: install linux-gpib and its Python bindings or gpib-ctypes (pip install gpib-ctypes)
diag_no_dev_gpib: {device} does not exist: the linux-gpib driver is not loaded/configured
diag_no_port: [GPIB-006] no serial port or network address is set for the adapter
hint_windows_keysight: Windows: install the Keysight IO Libraries Suite, plug the adapter in and check in Keysight Connection Expert which interface it is (GPIB0, GPIB1...). With NI-VISA installed too, enable 'VISA coexistence' or set the IVI backend.
hint_linux_keysight: Linux: install linux-gpib, set board_type = "agilent_82357a" in /etc/gpib.conf, load the firmware (gpib_config / fxload with the linux-gpib firmware package), then pip install gpib-ctypes and use the pyvisa-py backend (@py).
hint_windows_ni: Windows: install NI-VISA and NI-488.2, plug the adapter in and check its interface number (GPIB0...) in NI MAX.
hint_linux_ni: Linux: install linux-gpib, set board_type = "ni_usb_b" in /etc/gpib.conf, run gpib_config, then pip install gpib-ctypes and use the pyvisa-py backend (@py).
hint_windows_generic: Windows: install the VISA library of the adapter's maker and check the interface number (GPIB0...) in its configuration utility.
hint_linux_generic: Linux: configure the adapter in linux-gpib (/etc/gpib.conf, gpib_config) and use the pyvisa-py backend (@py) with gpib-ctypes.
hint_prologix_serial: The adapter appears as a serial port (COMx on Windows, /dev/ttyUSBx or /dev/ttyACMx on Linux). On Linux add your user to the 'dialout' group.
hint_prologix_ethernet: Set the IP address of the adapter (Prologix NetFinder); the tool connects to TCP port 1234.
